messages:
mike: Quick heads-up — I ran a profiling sweep on the multi-GPU serving job (8x H100, TP+DP) and observed a regression when fabric falls back to PCIe. Throughput down ~22%, tail latency spikes on generate paths. KV cache hit-rate looks normal, but prefetched KV reads show 2-3x latency variance. Posting sampling snippets and rough microbench numbers below. :eyes:

sophia: Is this across racks or within the same host? Any topology changes recently?

mike: Same rack, one node boundary crossing (4 GPUs/nodae -> other node 4 GPUs). We had a kernel selector tweak landed yesterday (commit ab12f6c) that changes quantized matmul kernel for head_dim=64. Repro steps: run inference load with 1k concurrent prefixes and prefetch enabled.

mike: Sample from perf trace (trimmed):
```
# start 1823460001
NCCL_ALLREDUCE  size=1MB  time_ms=2.5  (cross-node via EFA)
NCCL_ALLREDUCE  size=1MB  time_ms=0.7  (nvlink pairs)
KV_PREFETCH_READ  count=120k  p50=0.9ms  p95=4.2ms  p99=8.1ms
matmul_quant_head64_kernel=matmul_v2 (fallback path shows generic_matmul)
CPU->GPU memcpy small=512B time=0.25ms (many tiny copies)
```

raj: Looks like two issues mixing: (1) kernel selection fallback adding compute stalls, (2) cross-node fabric path increasing all-reduce latency. Did you run nccl-tests/ibv_perf to confirm raw fabric numbers? Might be rdma registration or pinned buffer choices.

clare: The kernel selector change replaced the head-optimized quant kernel with a more generalizable path for batched sequences. If small sequence lengths dominate, the selector chooses generic_matmul which is slower for head_dim=64. We saw a perf win in some long-seq tests but not in short-seq chat workloads. Maybe selector heuristic needs seq_len*batch weighting.

ben: I ran quick nccl microbench on the same nodes:
```
# nccl-tests allreduce 1MB
- GPUs with NVLink: 0.6 ms
- GPUs only via PCIe (same host but NVLink missing): 1.8 ms
- Cross-node via EFA (10Gb RDMA carve): 2.9 ms
```
So cross-node EFA is roughly 4-5x NVLink for 1MB. Allreduce overhead is significant for our shard sizes.

mike: Good numbers. On the serving stack the runtime does small allreduces many times (KV shard sync + cache invalidation). The perf regression seems amplified because compute got slightly slower (kernel fallback) so relative time spent waiting on comm grows and we lose overlap.

raj: Two practical suggestions: enable P2P NVLink where available (cuda deviceEnablePeerAccess), and adjust NCCL environ to prefer intra-node rings first. Also try NCCL_ALGO=Tree for medium sizes to reduce latency.

clare: For kernel selection: propose adding a quick cost model estimate where estimated_compute_ms = kernel_pref_cost(head_dim, seq_len, batch) and estimated_comm_ms = nccl_est(size) — choose kernel that minimizes max(compute, comm) to maximize overlap. Pseudocode: 
```
if estimated_compute > estimated_comm:
  pick fastest_compute_kernel
else:
  pick comm-friendly smaller-buffer kernel
```
Will open a PR to instrument estimator counters.

ben: Also worth trying to coalesce KV prefetch into larger batched reads to reduce many tiny CPU->GPU copies. We saw memcpy overhead of ~0.25ms per small copy; coalescing ~8x reduces that wall time.

mike: Reproduced locally by forcing kernel override: REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=generic_matmul and running the load — tail p99 increases by ~30%. If I force matmul_v1 (old fast path) the p99 returns to baseline. Commit ab12f6c is suspect.

sophia: @clare can you run a controlled AB test on canary (2 nodes) with kernel rollback vs current? infra-bot: schedule canary cluster? :rocket:

infra-bot: Canary cluster provisioned: canary-8h100-01. Run ID: canary-182346. Logs forwarded to #eng-runtime/canary-ops.

clare: I'll push a canary with kernel rollback and the estimator flags. Also adding extra telemetry: per-kernel compute time, nvlink/pcie path used per allreduce, and per-prefetch memcpy hist.

mike: Thanks. If we confirm kernel is main cause we'll ship a targeted revert + add heuristic to prefer matmul_v1 for head_dim==64 until we have better cost model. Also follow-up: evaluate RDMA tuning (buffer registration, GPUDirect RDMA) — if EFA perf is poor we may need infra-side tuning.

ben: One more data point: enabling async allreduce (kick off reduce earlier) reduced stall by ~12% in microbench. Might be a short-term mitigation while we fix kernel.

raj: Agree. I'll draft a runbook: check NVLink topology, nccl topo, memcopy counts, and kernel selection tag. Add a screenshot of nvidia-smi topo --matrix to the runbook.

mike: Great. I'll attach the full perf trace to the canary ticket and coordinate the AB. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
